curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: Start with the keep-right rule and its exceptions, define yielding, then show where the pavement tells you to stop or yield.
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: One card per lane-position rule; contrast cards for stop line versus yield line and keep right versus left-turn preparation.
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: Hub-chosen quiz on when you may leave the right side and what yielding requires.

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: Walk the statutory ladder from the narrowest streets upward, then the catch-all road limit and the interstate exception.
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: One card per statutory limit; contrast cards for narrow residential versus residential district and school zone versus residential.
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: Hub-chosen quiz that names a place and asks for its statutory limit.

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: Teach the basic rule as the everyday speed test, then sort the yellow advisory signs from the black-and-white limit signs, and close on why speed matters to pedestrians.
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: Rule cards for the basic rule; contrast cards for advisory versus limit signs and speed limit versus basic rule.
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: Hub-chosen quiz on whether a described speed is legal for the conditions and which signs are enforceable.

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: Explain what yellow means, then each center-line pattern and its passing rule, then the shared left-turn lane, the painted median and diagonal stripes.
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: One card per yellow pattern; contrast cards for your side versus the other side and turn lane versus painted median.
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: Hub-chosen quiz that describes a center-line pattern and asks whether you may pass, turn or drive there.

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: Rank the white lines from freely crossable to forbidden, explain the dotted line by location, then cover bike lanes, chevrons and red transit lanes.
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: One card per white or red marking; contrast cards for the crossing rules and for solid versus striped red.
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: Hub-chosen quiz on whether a described white or red marking may be crossed.

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: Define the space cushion, give the seconds rule and how to count it, then list when to add distance and what drives stopping distance.
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: Rule cards for the seconds gap and the counting method; list cards for the add-distance situations.
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: Hub-chosen quiz on the right gap for a speed and when a gap must grow.

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: Cover space beside you, then how to manage the driver behind you, then the head-turn backing routine.
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: One card per side or rear space rule; contrast cards for gradual slowing versus brake-checking and mirrors versus head turn.
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: Hub-chosen quiz on the right response to a tailgater, a merging car or a parked car.

learning_path_rule.rule: module order sec03-m01..sec03-m07; component facts before the synthesis (R) nodes that contrast them; no dynamic nodes exist

node_types.definition: one accepted handbook fact as an atomic node
one accepted C2 contrast fact joining the component facts it names

edge_types.definition: component fact must be learned before the contrast or dependent fact

domain_emphasis_check.domain: Lane travel, speed, pavement markings and space cushion

sequencing.rule: module order, then component facts before synthesis nodes
